title: Crossed signs (ipsilateral LMN facial + contralateral hemiparesis): pontine lesion
vignette: A 64-year-old man with a history of uncontrolled hypertension comes to the emergency department due to sudden-onset, right-sided weakness. Blood pressure is 170/106 mm Hg. Examination shows left facial weakness affecting the forehead and lower face. Muscle strength is 3/5 in the right upper and lower extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are brisk and Babinski sign is present on the right. A midline, sagittal section of a normal brain is shown, with labeled points: A = cortex, B = midbrain, C = cerebellum, D = pons, and E = medulla. This patient's lesion is most likely located at which of the following anatomic locations?

clues.text: left facial weakness affecting the forehead and lower face
clues.note: Facial weakness involving the FOREHEAD (whole hemiface) is a LOWER motor neuron (CN VII) pattern - localizing to the facial nerve nucleus/fascicle in the PONS on the LEFT.

clues.text: Muscle strength is 3/5 in the right upper and lower extremities
clues.note: Contralateral (right) arm and leg weakness with brisk reflexes and a Babinski sign is an UPPER motor neuron pattern from the corticospinal tract (before it decussates in the medulla).

clues.text: A = cortex, B = midbrain, C = cerebellum, D = pons, and E = medulla
clues.note: On the labeled midsagittal brain, D marks the PONS - where a lesion produces ipsilateral CN VII palsy with contralateral hemiparesis (crossed signs).

whatMatters: 'CROSSED SIGNS' - IPSILATERAL (left) LOWER-motor-neuron FACIAL palsy (forehead involved) plus CONTRALATERAL (right) UMN hemiparesis - localize to the LEFT PONS, where the CN VII nucleus lies and the corticospinal tract runs before decussating. That is point D. Answer D.
strategy: Use crossed signs to localize to the brainstem: cranial nerve deficit is IPSILATERAL to the lesion (CN VII forehead-involving = LMN = pons), body weakness is CONTRALATERAL (corticospinal tract above the medullary decussation). Left CN VII + right hemiparesis = left pons (D). Reject cortex A (UMN facial spares forehead; no crossed CN sign), midbrain B (CN III - ptosis/down-and-out eye), cerebellum C (ataxia/nystagmus), and medulla E (CN IX-XII - tongue/dysphagia/hoarseness).

eliminations.label: Cortex - UMN facial spares the forehead
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a cortical (or internal capsule) lesion. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes a CONTRALATERAL UPPER motor neuron facial palsy that SPARES the forehead (bilateral cortical input to the upper face) - not this forehead-involving (LMN) palsy or crossed signs. ✅ Correct if: contralateral face+body weakness with forehead sparing.

eliminations.label: Midbrain - CN III (down-and-out eye, ptosis)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a midbrain lesion. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it classically involves the oculomotor nerve (CN III), causing ipsilateral ptosis and a 'down-and-out' eye with contralateral hemiparesis (Weber), not a CN VII facial palsy. ✅ Correct if: CN III palsy + contralateral weakness.

eliminations.label: Cerebellum - ataxia/nystagmus, no crossed weakness
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a cerebellar lesion. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes ipsilateral ataxia, dysmetria, and nystagmus - not cranial nerve palsies with contralateral hemiparesis. ✅ Correct if: limb/gait ataxia, intention tremor.

eliminations.label: Medulla - CN IX-XII (tongue, dysphagia, hoarseness)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a medullary lesion. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: medullary strokes involve CN IX (gag), X (dysphonia), and XII (tongue), often with crossed sensory/motor findings - not a CN VII facial palsy. ✅ Correct if: tongue deviation/dysphagia/hoarseness (medial/lateral medullary syndromes).

reasoning: Forehead-involving (LMN) left facial weakness localizes to the left CN VII nucleus in the pons
Right-sided UMN hemiparesis reflects the corticospinal tract above its medullary decussation
Ipsilateral cranial nerve deficit + contralateral body weakness = crossed signs of a brainstem (pontine) lesion
mechanism: Because most cranial nerves (other than CN II and IV) do NOT decussate while the body's major motor (corticospinal) and sensory fibers DO cross in the medulla, BRAINSTEM strokes produce 'CROSSED SIGNS': an IPSILATERAL cranial-nerve deficit with CONTRALATERAL hemiparesis/hemisensory loss. The FACIAL nerve (CN VII) nucleus and fascicle lie in the PONS; a lesion there causes an IPSILATERAL LOWER motor neuron facial palsy affecting the WHOLE hemiface (forehead included) - distinguishing it from a cortical UPPER motor neuron palsy that SPARES the forehead (the upper face has bilateral cortical innervation). The corticospinal tract runs through the pons before decussating in the caudal medulla, so a pontine lesion also weakens the CONTRALATERAL arm and leg (UMN pattern: weakness, hyperreflexia, upgoing Babinski). This patient (uncontrolled hypertension - a risk for lacunar/pontine stroke) has LEFT LMN facial palsy + RIGHT hemiparesis = a LEFT PONTINE lesion, labeled D on the midsagittal brain. Cortex spares the forehead; midbrain gives CN III; cerebellum gives ataxia; medulla gives CN IX-XII deficits.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Neuro > brainstem localization: crossed signs (ipsilateral CN deficit + contralateral hemiparesis); CN VII nucleus = pons (LMN facial palsy, forehead involved); corticospinal decussates in medulla; cortical facial palsy spares forehead; midbrain = CN III, medulla = CN IX-XII.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Ipsilateral forehead-involving facial palsy + contralateral hemiparesis = pons.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on crossed signs, LMN vs UMN facial palsy, corticospinal decussation, or brainstem cranial nerve levels? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Cortex UMN facial spares forehead; midbrain = CN III; cerebellum = ataxia; medulla = CN IX-XII.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Midsagittal brain (stem, labeled A-E): the lesion localizes to D = PONS (CN VII nucleus + corticospinal tract before medullary decussation).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: crossed signs = brainstem; pons = ipsilateral CN VII (forehead) palsy + contralateral hemiparesis.

keywords.front: Ipsilateral forehead-involving facial palsy + contralateral hemiparesis

keywords.back: UMN spares forehead (cortical); LMN affects whole hemiface (CN VII/pons)
CN IX, X, XII (dysphagia, dysphonia, tongue)

firstAid.detail: Neuro: ipsilateral CN VII (forehead) + contralateral hemiparesis.

memoryHook: Whole-face droop on one side + arm/leg weakness on the other = a crossed (brainstem) sign at the pons (where CN VII lives and the motor tract hasn't crossed yet).
